Lautaro finishes 22nd as Kane wins the Ballon d'Or

First draft ran 581 prose words with a length WARN and a 34-word opening (subject plus the first dek sentence read as one sentence). Shortened the opening sentence and trimmed six places: the 2024 best-placing clause, the Sky Go/NOW detail, the Manchester City line, the Dimarco/Diouf sentence, the assistant referees and the fourth official. 495 words, 0 WARN. Editor read caught a dangling 'He' closing the Ballon d'Or item whose nearest antecedent was Yamal, not Martinez; rewritten with the name. 'France Football' glossed as 'the French magazine France Football' so an American reader does not read it as the country. Harry Kane's role moved into the dek so his first mention carries it. Not printed: Zebrauskas's contract to 2029 (announced by his agency on Instagram, not the club, and an Under-17 player); Chivu's birthday and the Solo Noi film (soft); Venezia's betting odds (house rule). FCInter1908 returned robots_disallowed all morning, so the aggregator pass ran on FCInterNews only. No Chivu pre-Venezia press conference published at run time. Ballon d'Or podium: FCInterNews's headline says Kane beat 'Yamal and Mbappe' while its body ranks Mbappe second and Yamal third, and SportMediaset's sidebar says Kane beat Mbappe narrowly; the edition prints the body order attributed to FCInterNews, because inter.it names no winner and only confirms Lautaro's 22nd. SEND: every hard control A1-H passed and the page went live, but the 5:30 AM run's sendNow call was blocked by that run's own permission classifier (Real-World Transactions) before reaching Brevo, and the campaign was left as a verified draft, not retried. Same refusal as the No. 55 run - the cause is that an unattended scheduled run has nobody to approve a send-class action, not Brevo or Composio. The owner then asked for a retry; campaign 45 was confirmed still 'draft' immediately before the call, so no duplicate was possible, and Brevo answered 204 and moved it to in_process at 12:34 PM ET. Sent once.
